label: rem:crossing-energy-categorical-origin
title: Crossing weights are Hecke eigenvalues, not postulates
html:
The per-crossing weights (q, -q^{-1}) of the crossing energy are not an energetic penalty laid on top of a topological framework. They are the two eigenvalues of the Hecke generator T = P \circ R \colon V \otimes V \to V \otimes V acting on the symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition. The rigid monoidal structure forces them:

  1. Rigidity fixes the R-matrix determinant. Dualisability of V and the categorical volume constraint (volume constraint) require the braiding R = c_{V,V} to satisfy \det(R|_{V \otimes V}) = 1, with eigenvalues (q, q^{-1}) on S^{2} V \oplus \Lambda^{2} V.
  2. The Hecke generator carries the transposition sign. The Hecke generator is T = P \circ R, where P is the swap. Since P|_{\Lambda^{2} V} = -\mathrm{id}, composition flips the sign on the antisymmetric summand. This gives T-eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) with \det(T) = -1, which matches the Hecke minimal polynomial (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 (eigenvalue extraction).
  3. Crossing weights are eigenvalues, not postulates. Assigning a positive crossing L_{+} the weight q and a negative crossing L_{-} the weight -q^{-1} represents precisely the action of T on a symmetric-channel input and T^{-1} on an antisymmetric-channel input. The sum \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) is therefore a trace of T^{\pm 1}-eigenvalues along the braid. The categorical structure dictates this assignment.
  4. Gröbner--Shirshov resolution. When \mathfrak{H} is reduced to Gröbner--Shirshov normal form, each crossing contributes its T-eigenvalue exactly once. The net \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} is the resulting Laurent polynomial in q, read off the normal form. Removing any of these weights would violate duality and break the Hecke relation.

Compute this quantity entirely from the R-matrix braiding (R-matrix) of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) acting on the tensor product of constituent representations.
